How we will measure canopy and shade

Canopy cover is the share of a fixed land area covered by the overhead projection of tree crowns. Overlapping crowns count once. We will record the imagery date, compare coverage with independent samples and report uncertainty. Changes require comparable imagery and a consistent denominator. We report mangrove extent, verified tree survival and afternoon pedestrian shade as separate measures.

Start with the WRI–Meta canopy height map, use Dynamic World to flag possible changes, and use Global Mangrove Watch for coastal context. Reference urban footprints against the GHSL Urban Centre Database.

OPEN TOOLS

How to build an atlas for your city

Start with a documented boundary and dated imagery. Use field observations to find out which trees the imagery misses and where people experience shade.

Map canopy

QGIS for inspecting imagery and tracing crowns. PostGIS for keeping boundaries, observations and releases.

Survey on foot

QField for coordinated offline surveys. Download the field observation template.

Process aerial images

OpenDroneMap for georeferenced mosaics from approved flights. DeepForest can help identify candidate crowns for review.

The Atlas source package contains the map, city roster, field template and a canopy calculation script for contributors.
